reference.title: Dumbbell Lying Rear Delt Row
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as you pull the elbows up and out, breathe in as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1.2 s up, short squeeze, about 2 s down

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; lighter than for a regular bent-over row (clinical opinion)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; slower lowering; chest-supported version to remove the low-back demand

cues.text: Lie face down on a high flat bench with the chin just past the end, legs straddling the bench, balls of the feet on the floor. Dumbbells hang under the shoulders, palms facing your feet.
Breathe out and pull the elbows up and out to the sides, wide of the body, keeping the chest on the bench.
Upper arms about level with the back, elbows bent about 90 degrees; squeeze the backs of the shoulders and the shoulder blades.
Breathe in and lower under control back to nearly straight arms.
Let the shoulder blades glide apart a little; chest stays down; repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the bench to heave the weight
mistakes.fix: Keep the chest on the pad; use lighter dumbbells.

mistakes.mistake: Elbows drifting back toward the hips
mistakes.fix: Pull the elbows out to the sides, in line with the shoulders.

mistakes.mistake: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
mistakes.fix: Keep the neck long; pull the shoulder blades back and down.
Keep the head in line with the trunk, eyes on the floor.

kinematics.norm: Chest supported on the bench so the low back does not hold a hinge; the bench is high enough that the dumbbells hang clear of the floor (clinical opinion; compare the lumbar demand of the free-standing bent-over row in Fenwick 2009)
Upper arm about 60-90 degrees out from the trunk so the pull is a horizontal abduction; horizontal abduction loads the posterior deltoid more than a close row (Franke 2015)
Nearly straight at the bottom, about 90 degrees at the top (clinical opinion)
Pronated (palms back) is the usual rear delt row grip; on a reverse fly a neutral grip gave more posterior deltoid activity than pronated (Schoenfeld 2013)
Legs straddle the bench, balls of the feet planted for balance (clinical opinion)
Controlled, about 1 s up and 2 s down (clinical opinion)

cautions: Use a stable bench; if you raise it on blocks or plates, make sure it cannot tip or slide.
Shoulder pain at the top: stop the elbows a little below the level of the back (clinical opinion).
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Low-back pain: the chest support usually makes this easier on the back than a bent-over version (clinical opinion).
No high bench: an incline bench at a low angle works the same way.

muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Prime mover: with the elbows out wide the row becomes a horizontal abduction (a bent-arm reverse fly). Horizontal abduction (reverse peck deck) gave much higher posterior deltoid activity than a close-elbow seated row (Franke 2015; Botton 2013).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Pull the shoulder blades together at the top of the row.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Pull the shoulder blades together at the top of the row.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: External rotator that works with the posterior deltoid in horizontal abduction (Schoenfeld 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Helps hold the upper arm out from the body as it rises.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Helps hold the upper arm out from the body as it rises.
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the elbow bend; less involved than in a close row because the elbows lead.
muscleNotes.core: Light bracing only: the bench holds the trunk (clinical opinion).
